summary: Bluff light above the Grand River mouth on Lake Erie, lit 1825; the 1871 sandstone tower held the light until 1925 and now houses a marine museum.

structures.note: Sandstone tower with brick-lined interior (LighthouseFriends); 60 ft to the lantern (Lighthouse Society place record). LighthouseFriends gives 68 ft for the same tower.
First tower with the 1825 lighthouse and dwelling, 55 ft (LighthouseFriends); taken down after a temporary light was shown on 10 December 1869.
Red brick, one and a half storeys, joined to the tower by an eighteen-foot covered passage (LighthouseFriends); the museum occupies it.

access.note: Grounds open; dwelling and tower open in season (LighthouseFriends). The Historical Society's keeper page gives museum hours as noon to 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday and legal holidays, Memorial Day to 30 September 2026.

facts.agency: Fairport Harbor Marine Museum (owner, per LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Lighthouse and keeper's dwelling built by Hiram Wood and Jonathan Goldsmith for $2,900
Fixed white light, fueled by whale oil, first exhibited in the fall
Congress appropriates $30,000 for a new tower and keeper's house; temporary light shown from 10 December 1869 while the old tower came down
New brick-lined tower and dwelling completed after the 1871 appropriation of $10,000
First shown from the new tower on 11 August 1871
Third-order Fresnel lens moved from the first tower into the new one
Water piped from the city water works into the keeper's dwelling; hand rail placed in the tower
Roof built over the covered way, fence around the grounds replaced, extensive repairs
Congress appropriates $42,000 (12 June 1917) for aids at Fairport Harbor, including a new light on the west breakwater pierhead; the 1915-1922 estimates had proposed discontinuing the bluff light
Bluff light discontinued when the west breakwater light was first lit on 9 June 1925
Lighthouse and keeper's dwelling turned into the Marine Museum; the museum opened in 1945 (LighthouseFriends)
Men's Civic Club of Fairport placed a bronze tablet on the old light inscribed 'Built 1825-Rebuilt 1871'; the Bulletin says the tower still remained, still owned by the Lighthouse Service
Listed on the National Register as Fairport Marine Museum (NRIS 71000642)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lighthouse Society's place record gives 60 ft from base to lantern for the 1871 tower; LighthouseFriends gives 68 ft for the same tower; the station record gives 18.0 m (about 59 ft). The story gives both published figures; the structure entry uses 18.3 m (60 ft).

resolved_conflicts.field: last year of Daniel I. Babcock
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The roster ends his head-keeper stint in 1925, the year the bluff light was discontinued; LighthouseFriends says he served until 1926. The roster date is used in the keeper line and the discrepancy is stated in the story.

The Archive lists keepers to 1944 under this place. The Bulletin of 1933 and the Archive's West Breakwater roster place the post-1925 keeping at the new breakwater light, so the bluff light's keeper list stops at 1925.

notes_for_editor: (1) Tower height: 60 ft to lantern (Lighthouse Society place record), 68 ft (LighthouseFriends), 18.0 m in the station record. Not resolved; the story gives both published figures. (2) The first (1825) tower: LighthouseFriends gives 55 ft for the lighthouse and dwelling. The Historical Society's home page gives 30 ft and octagonal lantern for the first tower; the home page is not a specific page, so it is not cited. Check with the Society before publishing a height for the 1825 tower. (3) Keepers after 1925 are left out of this station's roster; see resolved_conflicts. The Archive still lists them under this place. (4) The Underground Railroad account comes from the Historical Society's keeper page only; no primary source for escapes was read. LighthouseFriends names a tavern-keeping Samuel Butler (1850) who chaired an anti-slavery group; no source connects him to the keeper Samuel Butler (1825-1833, 1841-1845), so they are not linked. (5) Pierhead beacons and the east-pier range lights are separate aids on the Board's lists. The 1892 Canisteo gale is kept as harbour context, marked as not at the bluff light; the 1898 range-tower collision is not used. (6) The Life-Saving Station No. 7 wreck (17 November 1879, in the report for the fiscal year ending 30 June 1880) is near the harbour mouth and not tied to the light. (7) NRHP: NRIS 71000642 is titled Fairport Marine Museum, listed 5 November 1971, significant year 1871 (NPGallery). The nomination PDF is not digitised. (8) Corpus: the Board's annual reports in the corpus cover 1891 to 1901 only, so the 1825 to 1871 construction and the 1869 to 1871 appropriations rest on LighthouseFriends, not on primary reports read here. (9) Roster row Andrew A. Kocak has an end year (1921) and no start year in the archive. (10) The contractor Jonathan Goldsmith is on the roster as a contractor and is not counted as a keeper. (11) Hours differ: the Society's keeper page gives noon to 6 p.m. (Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun, legal holidays, Memorial Day to 30 Sept 2026); LighthouseFriends gives 1 to 6 p.m. (Wed, Sat, Sun, holidays; Memorial Day weekend to the third weekend in September). Both are stated in the story. (12) LighthouseFriends is an all-rights-reserved site: facts are paraphrased and quotations are kept to a few words. (13) Newspapers: Chronicling America search for 'Fairport' with 'lighthouse' in Ohio papers, 1871 to 1900, returned 23 pages, mostly directories and advertisements; none was read, so no newspaper account is used. The 1871 relighting and 1879-1898 incidents rest on the Board, Life-Saving and Commissioner reports. (14) Commissioner estimate, item 29 (scan p.89, printed p.84): the OCR reads 'to construct e new light'; the story prints 'a new light'. Confirm the word on the page image before publication. (15) Fiscal years: the Board entries for 1892 (water and handrail, scan p.526) and 1895 (roof over the covered way, scan p.359) are dated by fiscal year (July to June), because the report covers that year. The corpus labels the 1892 volume '1891-1892'; the entry's text refers to May 1892 events and to navigation in 1893, so it belongs to the report for the year ended 30 June 1892. (16) The Historical Society and LighthouseFriends disagree on the bluff light's visiting hours; the story states both.
